greenwood_accessible_bath_laundry.heading: Accessible ADA compliant Bathroom and Laundry Renovation in Greenwood
greenwood_accessible_bath_laundry.text1: This accessible ADA compliant bathroom and laundry renovation in Greenwood includes a curbless shower and a custom wheelchair-accessible vanity. The project needed to support multiple daily-use functions at once, including bathing, storage, circulation, privacy, and laundry access.
greenwood_accessible_bath_laundry.text2: The strongest part of the project is how much function was built into a limited footprint. Partial-height walls, the curbless shower, the custom wheelchair-accessible vanity, warm wood storage, laundry integration, and built-in shelving all work together so the room feels organized and cohesive instead of crowded.
greenwood_accessible_bath_laundry.short2: Accessible ADA compliant Bathroom and Laundry Renovation in Greenwood
greenwood_accessible_bath_laundry.text3: Explore how the shower, vanity, storage, laundry function, and finish details were coordinated within this compact footprint.

part1.small_heading: Compact layout planned for everyday use
part1.text2: This Greenwood project was clarified as a bathroom and laundry renovation because the space needed to solve more than a single bathroom update. The room had to support bathing, storage, circulation, privacy, and laundry-related utility in one compact footprint.
part1.text3: The laundry functions as a hallway into the bathroom, and two pocket doors divide the spaces for privacy. The layout uses partial-height divider walls to organize the room without closing it off completely. That separation helps the shower, vanity, toilet, and laundry zones each feel intentional while still keeping the overall space open and easy to move through.

part2.text2: The vanity was designed so that someone in a wheelchair can roll their knees under it while washing their hands. The vanity area gives the room a warmer and more custom feel. The wood counter, integrated sink, simple wall lights, and red trim detail help the space feel designed rather than treated as a basic utility room.
part2.text3: This is an important part of the project because compact bathrooms can easily feel purely functional. Here, the vanity adds visual character while still keeping the sink area practical for daily use.

part3.small_heading: Curbless accessible shower with durable tile work
part3.text2: The curbless shower provides step-free entry and was treated as a long-term performance space. Large-format wall tile, a glass partition, a handheld fixture, grab bars, and a bench make the shower more comfortable, durable, and easier to use.
part3.text3: The finished shower keeps the design simple and clean while adding practical features that support safety and day-to-day function. These details help the room feel more complete than a standard cosmetic remodel.

part4.small_heading: Toilet zone with upper storage and clean detailing
part4.text2: The toilet area was planned as its own finished zone rather than leftover space. The upper wood cabinet provides useful storage, while the surrounding wall surfaces, fixture placement, and accessories keep the area clean and organized.
part4.text3: This kind of detail matters in a smaller bathroom and laundry room because every wall and corner has to work harder. Storage, privacy, and fixture placement all contribute to making the room feel considered from end to end.

part5.small_heading: A laundry hallway with two pocket doors
part5.text2: The laundry component is one of the reasons this project should be described as more than a bathroom remodel. Appliance placement, clearances, floor durability, access, and storage all had to be considered within the hallway leading into the bathroom.
part5.text3: The completed space shows the laundry function as part of the overall plan rather than an afterthought. It supports real household use while still maintaining the finish quality expected in a renovated bathroom.

part6.small_heading: Shelving, lighting, and finish details complete the room
part6.text2: Built-in shelving, wood doors, tile flooring, lighting, and storage details help the room feel complete. The shelves add useful organization, while the warm wood tones and red edge accents connect the different parts of the room visually.
part6.text3: The final result is a compact bathroom and laundry space that balances utility with design. The project shows how a small service area can become a polished, organized, and durable part of the home.
